authorization: Publisher explicitly authorised three verified daily company-analysis articles on 2 November 2026, superseding the repository's one-new-article daily cap.
story_thesis: Fee revenue is compounding faster than rooms through RevPAR and card economics, while repurchases exceed cash after capital spending and make rising debt part of the per-share story.

identity.units: USD millions except per-share, percentage, property and room data

duplicate_checks: Checked EDITORIAL_TOPIC_INDEX.md, CONTENT_INVENTORY.md, data/content-inventory.json and actual wealth Markdown; Marriott has a stock profile but no dedicated fee-growth/capital-return analysis.
Checked recent company-publication records, merged and open pull requests, and live site content; no matching Marriott story or fingerprint was active or published.
Routine results remain on /stocks/mar/; this article addresses asset-light fee compounding and capital allocation.

evidence_table.claim: Q3 franchise and base-management fees were USD1.341bn, up 13%, and incentive-management fees USD181m, up 22%.
evidence_table.location_or_arithmetic: Release Q3 results and 10-Q fee-revenue MD&A.

evidence_table.claim: Worldwide RevPAR grew 6.5%, comprising 4.8% ADR growth and 1.1 percentage points of occupancy improvement.
evidence_table.result: verified; RevPAR identified as a company performance measure

evidence_table.claim: Quarter-end system had 1,833,801 rooms, up about 4.6% from 1,753,722 a year earlier; pipeline exceeded 634,000 rooms with 44% under construction.
evidence_table.result: verified; more than 37,000 approved pipeline rooms lacked signed contracts

evidence_table.claim: Higher co-branded card fees added USD68m to quarterly franchise-fee growth, while RevPAR and room growth added USD36m.
Nine-month operating cash flow was USD3.239bn, capital and technology expenditure USD411m, share repurchases USD3.081bn and dividends USD559m.
evidence_table.location_or_arithmetic: 10-Q sources and uses of cash; 3,239 - 411 = 2,828, below 3,081 + 559 = 3,640.
evidence_table.result: verified; broader investment spending distinguished from capex

evidence_table.claim: Total debt was USD16.8bn versus USD16.2bn at 2025 year end; cash was about USD0.4bn and net long-term debt issuance/repayment provided USD1.451bn year to date.
evidence_table.location_or_arithmetic: Release liquidity paragraph and 10-Q cash-flow/debt notes.
evidence_table.result: verified; no unsupported net-debt measure used

fact_check_pass.method: After drafting, every material number, period, fee category, performance measure, management explanation and calculation was reread against the official release and Form 10-Q; arithmetic was independently recomputed.
